value: Tokac, B., Zhang, Q. and Sari, Y.A. (2025). Environmental and economic comparison of diesel and electric trucks in open-pit mining operations. Journal of Cleaner Production 507, 145540. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2025.145540

Discrete-event simulation of 16 diesel versus battery-electric CAT 777D trucks in a hypothetical Sudbury open pit. Loaded: per-minute fuel/electricity rates for road segments (the only energy intensities printed; annual tonnage is not given so no per-tonne or per-t-km values exist), fleet annual operating costs (diesel 10.4 M, electric 4.0 M, 6.3 M with battery replacement), derived per-truck values, efficiencies, battery cost and life, emission reduction. Not loaded: capital cost (not studied), segment-by-segment values shown only in figures (Figs 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15), SI tables S1-S7 (not in the PDF). Locator: printed page = PDF page. Traps: currency of the $ values is not stated (diesel 1.14 $/L, electricity 0.09 $/kWh; USD assumed because battery cost is given in US$); no price year; the text gives crusher idle 0.02 L/min but Fig. 8 shows about 0.036; Table 1 efficiencies are model drivetrain factors not engine efficiency; energy efficiency 75-85 % (diesel) is used with the 35 % engine efficiency from the introduction quoted separately.
